A held-out step that runs through a screen no merged ticket has built is not run, not red
why: A step author writes browser steps from the brief, so a step can open a card page or a chat pane that a later ticket builds. Such a step fails on the missing screen, not on the ticket's code, and the follow-up it files asks a builder to build another ticket's work or to change nothing. The step can only say something once the ticket that builds the screen is merged.

To keep a red step pointing at merged code (see #st-heldout-merged-only), a step that needs a screen, a route or a pane that no merged ticket provides ends as not run (see #st-heldout-notrun). It files no follow-up. G2 still waits for it, and the held-out run after each later merge tries it again, so the step goes green or red once the ticket that builds the screen merges.

The ticket's own behaviour is still checked on the main line: its unit tests pin the same paths at the seam the ticket builds, such as the renderer for a ticket that renders card text.

Example:

- Ticket R "Card text renders Markdown with live card links" builds the renderer and is merged.
- Ticket P "A card page shows the card as a hero box" builds the card page and is still blocked.

No. The same cause also produces other cases.

- **Screens:** #st-heldout-unbuilt-screen covers a step that opens a page or pane that no merged ticket built. That card is still a proposal.
- **Operations and screens have no other owner.** Operations and screens are the two ways a step reaches the product today, so only they have a card.
- **Other missing capabilities:** A step can also need a field or event kind in the log, a server route, a card kind, or a behaviour of the agent. A later ticket builds each of these. Today they would file the same repeat follow-up.

The shared cause is this: the step needs a capability that no merged ticket provides. The step fails on the missing capability, not on the ticket's code. The operation case and the screen case are two ways the binder can detect it.

I see two options:

1. **One general card (recommended).** "A step that needs a capability no merged ticket has built is not run, not red." The binder reports the missing capability. Operations and screens become the two worked examples on that card.
2. **Keep two cards, add one per new kind.** Each card stays small. A third kind later needs a third card.

If you pick option 1, I discard the two proposals and propose one card in their place. #st-heldout-notrun stays the parent.

Next: choose option 1 or 2.

card st-heldout-unbuilt-op-close  [decided]  PROPOSED — not in the map until it is accepted
A follow-up whose every step needs an unbuilt command-line operation closes with no code change
why: A follow-up ticket can hold only held-out steps that start a build pass, a chat or a sample before any merged ticket built that operation. No change inside the follow-up can make those steps pass, and the behaviour behind them is already checked by unit tests at the seam an earlier ticket built. Each further builder pass costs a run and ends on the same finding.

To stop a follow-up from looping on work that belongs to another ticket, a builder pass on it checks two facts. First, each of its steps starts an operation that the command line does not provide on the main line. Second, the seam behind each step has unit tests that state the step's outcome, and those tests pass on the main line. When both facts hold, the pass ends with no code change, and the grader scores each acceptance criterion as met: the step is not run (see #st-heldout-notrun), not failed. The steps stay in the held-out set, G2 still waits for them, and the held-out run after each later merge tries them again. A step that goes red once its operation exists files a new follow-up then (see #st-heldout-followup-per-ticket). When a step lacks a passing unit test at its seam, the pass writes that test, and does not close on the first fact alone.

The guideline chose this answer by no data deleted and easiest to undo: no step leaves the held-out set, and a later red result files a fresh follow-up. It also needs no new link between tickets, which is the smallest interface.

- Follow-up F holds R's steps S1 "a build pass starts with the instructions" and S2 "a sample agent gets no instructions".

3. The pass ends with no code change. The grader scores both criteria as met. F closes.
4. B merges. The held-out run tries S1. S1 is green: nothing happens. S1 is red: a new follow-up for R is filed.

The coordinator runs the held-out set after each merge (#st-build-run). A red step files a follow-up ticket, and build goes on. The held-out set does not block the merge queue; only the checks do. G2 opens only when the full held-out set passes on the final merged tree.

So build ends later when held-out steps fail. It does not end with a known break in the pull request.

Yes. The map already decided a part of this, on 2026-10-20.

- **#st-heldout-merged-only** (decided) limits the held-out run after a merge to the steps of merged tickets. A red step must point at code on the main line.
